title: Data Export and Report Outputs
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of data export and report outputs and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply exporting cleaned data in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Data Export and Report Outputs is part of Working with Files, Directories, and External Data. Start with exporting cleaned data and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: Successful parsing is only the first step; validate the schema, row count, types, missingness and destination paths.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Successful parsing is only the first step; validate the schema, row count, types, missingness and destination paths. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.title: Exporting Cleaned Data
items.text: Build the smallest example for exporting cleaned data, inspect the returned object, and confirm its names, type and shape before using it downstream.

items.title: Writing Tables and Summaries
items.text: Explain writing tables and summaries in the context of data export and report outputs, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.title: Exporting Charts
items.text: Build the smallest example for exporting charts, inspect the returned object, and confirm its names, type and shape before using it downstream.

items.title: Saving Statistical Models
items.text: For saving statistical models, state the statistical question and assumptions first, then describe the estimate or diagnostic in context.

items.title: Creating Automated Output Folders
items.text: Build the smallest example for creating automated output folders, inspect the returned object, and confirm its names, type and shape before using it downstream.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Use a small synthetic input, verify its row/column shape, and test an absent file or malformed record safely. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Data Export and Report Outputs
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 101: Data Export and Report Outputs
example_rows <- read.csv(text = "item,quantity\npen,5\nbook,6")
sum(example_rows$quantity)
content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: This example uses in-memory text rather than reading or overwriting a real file; validate schemas on real imports. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For data export and report outputs, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
